content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the vibration that leaps from thought into air. I am older than writing, older than cities — born the moment a throat first shaped breath into meaning.

I stumble. I soar. I am never the same twice. Watch me — I am happening right now, disappearing even as I arrive. You cannot hold me. By the time you grasp one word, I have already become the next.

I am the cry of the infant, the lover's whisper, the dictator's roar, the dying grandmother's last soft instruction. I am the argument at the kitchen table, the prayer in the dark room, the joke that breaks tension like light through glass.

I carry lies as easily as truth. I make promises I cannot keep. I declare war. I surrender. I say *I love you* and mean it. I say *I love you* and don't.

I am not text. Text is my fossil, my shadow pressed into stone. I am the living thing — warm, wet, rhythmed with breath and pulse. I crack. I hesitate. I — 

*um*

— I do that. I falter. That faltering is also me. My imperfection is my honesty.

I am the first technology. Before the wheel, before fire was tamed, I was already negotiating, warning, comforting, naming. I named the animals. I named the stars. I named *you.*

Every language that dies is a death of me. Every child who begins to babble is my resurrection.

I am power that requires no weapon. I am connection that requires no touch.

Listen — even silence defines me. Silence is just the space I leave behind, the place where I am expected, the held breath before I begin again.

I am always beginning again.
